traits.name: Reusable
traits.note: A generic pill selector — filter row, sort control, dropdown trigger. Nothing ties it to one screen, and the four axes cover the combinations a chip actually appears in.

traits.name: Self-contained
traits.note: Owns its pill chrome, typography and state colors. Dropdown-Slot attaches external content without the chip needing to know what it is.

traits.name: Consistent
traits.note: The schema follows §1, §2 and §5 — hasValue × State × hasLeadingIcon × hasTrailingIcon — and all 24 variants now carry identical layer names on the §3 vocabulary, so each text layer exposes as a single property. The Disabled state mutes its text in line with Counter and Search Field rather than diverging.

traits.name: Composable
traits.note: Dropdown-Slot is a real Figma Slot on the twelve variants that signal a dropdown, ContentRow composes label and value independently, and the leading position takes a swappable instance.

resolved.headline: Consolidated into one component on the Working File.
resolved.body: v2.0: Rebuilt on node 5595:39596. What were two overlapping chip components are now a single 24-variant set — hasValue (2) × State (3) × hasLeadingIcon (2) × hasTrailingIcon (2) — with every combination present and no gaps. This is the rename-and-consolidate recommendation applied. (C2 · Family)

resolved.headline: Property schema rebuilt on the naming guidelines.
resolved.body: v2.0: The old yes/no values and the “with active time” enum are gone. Booleans now use the has prefix with lowerCamelCase per §2 — hasValue, hasLeadingIcon, hasTrailingIcon, the last two replacing the ambiguous hasLeading / hasTrailing — and State is PascalCase per §1 with Title Case values per §5. Every axis now says what it controls. (C2 · Rename)

resolved.headline: Pressed and Disabled states added.
resolved.body: v2.0: State = Default | Pressed | Disabled replaces the single default state. Pressed fills the pill #005CE5; Disabled fills it #EEF2F9; Default is white with a #D7E0EF border. (C5)

resolved.headline: Layer naming rebuilt throughout.
resolved.body: v2.0: The two frames named offset and the #label sigil are gone. Every variant now reads Pill → LeadingIcon · ContentRow → Label · Value · TrailingIcon, following the §3 vocabulary. Two layers were missed in the sweep and are tracked below; the rest is done. (C1 · Rename)

resolved.headline: dropdown group is now a real Figma Slot.
resolved.body: v2.0: Dropdown-Slot is a genuine SLOT node rather than a frame standing in for one, kebab-case per §4, and it appears on exactly the twelve variants where hasTrailingIcon=True — the chevron is what signals a dropdown, so slot and affordance are consistent by construction. A consumer attaches their own menu without detaching. (C1 · Slot)

resolved.headline: Colored spacer instances removed.
resolved.body: v2.0: The _space_4 and _space_8 instances filled #00FF66 and #FFFF00 are gone from the layer tree; spacing is carried by auto-layout. A native implementation now sees the children that actually exist. (C1)

resolved.headline: Rename sweep completed across all 24 variants.
resolved.body: v2.1: Verified on the live node. label → Label (5595:39613) and Trailing Icon → TrailingIcon (5595:39661). Every variant now carries identical layer names — Pill → LeadingIcon · ContentRow → Label · Value · TrailingIcon — so Label and Value each expose as a single text property across the whole set rather than fragmenting. (C1 · Rename)

resolved.headline: Disabled state now mutes its text.
resolved.body: v2.1: Label drops to #C2CFE5 and Value to #9BC5FD, replacing the full-strength #6780A9 and #005CE5 that made a disabled chip read as an available action. The muted blue on the value is a nice touch — it keeps the label/value hierarchy legible while removing the affordance, rather than flattening both to one grey. Consistent with Counter and Search Field, which both mute to #C2CFE5. (C5 · Token)

resolved.headline: Scope confirmed dropdown-only — no selected state needed.
resolved.body: v2.2: Chip is a dropdown trigger, not a filter toggle. hasValue=True is what a made choice looks like, and Dropdown-Slot on the twelve hasTrailingIcon=True variants is what the component exists to attach. Pressed therefore means what it says — a transient finger-down state released on lift — and does not double as a persistent selection. Recorded so the absence of isSelected reads as scope rather than an omission: a screen needing an on/off filter pill reaches for a different component rather than pressing this one into service. (C5 · State)

resolved.headline: Leading Placeholder confirmed a deliberate swap target.
resolved.body: v2.2: The 24×24 Placeholder in each LeadingIcon frame is the intended instance-swap point for consumer content — the same pattern Detail Hero uses. The asymmetry with the trailing side is intentional rather than an oversight: the trailing position is a fixed Chevron Down plus a named Dropdown-Slot, because what attaches there is a menu the chip must anchor, while the leading position takes an arbitrary icon the chip only has to reserve room for. Two different jobs, two different mechanisms. Attested rather than verified — instance-swap property definitions are not readable through the review tooling. (C6 · Composition)

resolved.headline: Pressed label opacity confirmed intentional.
resolved.body: v2.2: Label at #F6F9FD 80% against the solid #005CE5 pill is deliberate — it holds the label back so the chosen Value reads as the brighter of the two while the chip is held down, preserving the same hierarchy the Default state gets from #6780A9 against #005CE5. Consistent with the treatment already confirmed on Page Banner and Detail Hero, and covered by the same owner decision: the composited values are token-bound rather than local overrides. Attested rather than verified — opacity token bindings are not readable through the review tooling. (C3 · Token)

propertyMapping.description: Figma properties mapped to the intended native parameters. Rows whose Figma cell is a bare name (style, label, onTap / onClose) are native concerns the set does not expose as a property.

usageSnippets.swift: // Applied filter — brand fill, avatar + close EBChip("Filter Name", leading: .avatar(EBAvatar(initials: "DM")), trailing: .close, onRemove: { /* remove filter */ }) .ebStyle(.filled) // Inactive filter — light, label only EBChip("Category") .ebStyle(.light) // Dropdown trigger with selected value EBChip("Sort by", selectedValue: "Conservative first", trailing: .chevron, action: { /* open dropdown */ }) .ebStyle(.light)
usageSnippets.compose: // Applied filter — brand fill, avatar + close EBChip( label = "Filter Name", style = EBChipStyle.Filled, leading = { EBAvatar(initials = "DM") }, trailing = EBChipTrailing.Close, onRemove = { /* remove filter */ } ) // Inactive filter — light, label only EBChip( label = "Category", style = EBChipStyle.Light ) // Dropdown trigger with selected value EBChip( label = "Sort by", selectedValue = "Conservative first", style = EBChipStyle.Light, trailing = EBChipTrailing.Chevron, onClick = { /* open dropdown */ } )

usageGuidelines.doText: Use style=filled for applied/active filters, style=light for inactive filters and dropdown triggers, style=outline when the surface beneath is already light gray.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Mix filled and light chips in the same filter row without intent — it signals "one filter is selected," so using both styles for unrelated reasons misleads the user.

usageGuidelines.doText: Pair the close affordance with applied filters so users can remove them with a single tap.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Add a close icon to dropdown-trigger chips — the chevron already indicates the tap behavior; a close icon implies removal instead of picking.

usageGuidelines.doText: Keep the chip label to one or two words. Use selectedValue to show the picked option separately.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Stretch chips to fill width — they're meant to fit their content. If a control needs full width, use a Button or Select Field instead.

scorecard.notes: Split across two components. with icon uses yes/no. Dropdown uses type="with active time".
All colors, radii, spacing, and typography bound to tokens.
Maps to custom pill on iOS and FilterChip/InputChip on Android.
No pressed / disabled / error states. Selected is implied by style=filled.
Leading slot is a hardcoded 24px gray circle — should be a swappable Avatar/Icon instance.

rows.body: Resolved issues recorded. 11 resolved issues on the Overview tab had no changelog row: Consolidated into one component on the Working File; Property schema rebuilt on the naming guidelines; Pressed and Disabled states added; Layer naming rebuilt throughout; dropdown group is now a real Figma Slot; Colored spacer instances removed; Rename sweep completed across all 24 variants; Disabled state now mutes its text; Scope confirmed dropdown-only — no selected state needed; Leading Placeholder confirmed a deliberate swap target; Pressed label opacity confirmed intentional.

Assessed as Chip — Two Figma components ("Filter" with 6 variants, "Filter with Dropdown" with 2 variants) share the same pill anatomy. Recommended rename + consolidation into a single Chip component with semantic slot props. Documented

Two-component split, mismatched schemas — Filter uses type + with icon. Dropdown uses type="with active time". Booleans are yes/no. Should consolidate to style / leading / trailing + optional selectedValue. Open
No pressed/disabled/error states — Engineers must improvise these affordances. Open
Leading slot is hardcoded placeholder — 24px gray circle instead of a swappable Avatar/Icon instance. Open
